title: Whole Grain Pasta with Tomato Sauce and Poultry

content.title: About
content.content: Whole grain pasta with tomato sauce and pieces of poultry is a home recipe created in 2023. Whole grain pasta retains most of the bran and germ, making it more nutritious than traditional white pasta. The tomato sauce, made from ripe tomatoes, olive oil, and aromatic herbs, gives the dish a bright flavor, while tender poultry adds extra protein.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole grain pasta contains twice as much fiber as regular white pasta.
Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, which becomes more bioavailable after cooking.
The poultry used is often free‑range, increasing its omega‑3 fatty acid content.
Traditional Italian marinara sauce is a common base for similar tomato sauces.
Making the sauce at home lets you control the amount of salt and sugar.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Whole grain pasta provides dietary fiber that supports healthy digestion and blood sugar regulation.

items.title: Lycopene and antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes in the sauce contain lycopene, which helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Whole grain pasta has a lower glycemic index than white pasta, beneficial for weight management.

items.title: Protein from poultry
items.content: Lean poultry offers high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both the whole grain pasta and tomato sauce supply B1, B3, and B6 vitamins, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Whole grain pasta contains gluten, so individuals with celiac disease should choose gluten‑free alternatives.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Tomato sauce can be salty; monitor added salt to keep sodium intake moderate.

items.title: Potential poultry pathogens
items.content: Poultry must be cooked thoroughly to avoid risks of salmonella and campylobacter.

items.title: Tomato acidity
items.content: People with acid reflux may experience discomfort from the acidic tomato sauce.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook the pasta until al dente, then toss with hot tomato sauce and sautéed poultry pieces. Sprinkle with grated Parmesan, fresh basil, or oregano. Serve with a green salad or vegetable side dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry whole grain pasta in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Keep cooked sauce and finished dishes in the refrigerator for up to 3 days, or freeze portions for up to 2 months.
